The hidden cost of hand soldering

Angled joints, dense boards and drifting hands — the S-HX331R answers all three

Hand soldering struggles exactly where the S-HX331R is strongest: rotary access to angled joints, consistent temperature on dense boards, and solder fed by program instead of by feel.

Angled joints defeat manual routines

Side-entry and rotated joints force operators into awkward tip angles that are hard to repeat and easy to get wrong.

Dense boards punish hesitation

On high-density boards, dwell time decides between a cold joint and a bridge. Hands hesitate; the machine does not.

Temperature drifts under load

An iron cools at every joint. Operators compensate by pressing harder, and the PCB pays the price.

Solder feeding is guesswork

Too much wire balls the joint; too little starves it. Hand feeding cannot hit the same fillet twice.

Defects surface at test

Cold joints and bridges hide until electrical test — the most expensive place to discover them.

Labor cost compounds

Three workers per soldering task is the manual baseline; headcount, wages and turnover all climb with volume.

Installation guide

From bench to production in five steps

Installation and training are included free with every S-HX331R.

01 · Bench & fixture

Place the robot on a stable workbench. We design the PCB fixture to your boards — panel size, support points and clearance for the tip.

02 · Utilities

Connect 220 V mains power (full-voltage AC110–220 V on the S-HX331R). No compressed air is required for standard operation; prepare soldering wire and tips.

03 · Programming

Set soldering temperature (0–500 °C), teach paths with the handheld teaching box, and store programs — capacity for more than 100 sets.

04 · Trial run

Solder sample boards, then tune temperature, feed speed and tip height until every joint passes your acceptance criteria.

05 · Training & ramp

Free installation and operator training included; 24/7 worldwide support and 1-day spare-part lead time after handover.

Technical evaluation FAQ

Questions buyers ask before ordering

What makes the S-HX331R a four-axis robot?

It combines the Z axis (vertical) with an R rotary axis, giving a 360° soldering range on top of the X and Y travels. Angled and side-entry joints are soldered in the same program instead of being re-fixtured.

What is the 'broken tin' function?

The solder breaker cracks the oxidized outer layer of the solder wire before feeding, so the fresh solder core reaches the nozzle. Combined with program-controlled feed timing, it produces consistent fillets with less wire waste.

How fast and how accurate is it?

Movement speed from 0 to 800 mm/s with ±0.02 mm repeat accuracy and 0.01 mm/s control resolution. It is fast enough for volume and precise enough for dense, fine-pitch THT boards.

Can it connect to our systems?

Yes — the RS232 external control interface connects the robot to PLCs and MES data flow, and DVR video plus HDMI output support live observation and audits.

What utilities does it need?

Full-voltage AC110–220 V mains power; no compressed air required for standard operation. The robot weighs 69 kg and sits on a stable workbench with your PCB fixture.

How do I get a price and ROI estimate?

Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your board samples or drawings, joint count per board and monthly volume. Configuration, quotation and ROI estimate are provided after technical confirmation — typically within 24 hours.
